title: Extension by zero on the pro-etale site
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. For an open immersion
$j:U\hookrightarrow X$, extension by zero on the small pro-etale
site (the functor $j_!$ of [def-weil-extension-by-zero])
is the exact left adjoint of $j^{-1}$, acts degreewise, and
has the same stalk prescription as the etale one,

$$
(j_!K)_{\bar x}=
\begin{cases}
K_{\bar x},&\bar x\text{ lies in }U,\\
0,&\bar x\text{ lies in }X\setminus U,
\end{cases}
$$

for a complex $K$ of sheaves of $A$-modules on $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and a geometric point
$\bar x$ of $X$; it is compatible with restriction of scalars
along a homomorphism $A\to B$ of finite commutative rings [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]: canonically $\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B}j_!^B K\cong j_!^A\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B}K$ for a complex $K$ of $B$-module sheaves.

proof.text: The localization and coefficient identifications in [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], for the open immersion $j$, identify $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ and $A_U$ with $A_X|_U$. Apply [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] with $\mathcal C=X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $\mathcal O=A_X$: its sheafified extension-by-zero presheaf is exactly [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. It gives exactness of both restriction and $j_!$, and the module-sheaf adjunction $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$.

source.place: Lemmas Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact), with proetale.tex Definition Tag 09AE (definition-extension-zero); specialization to the open-immersion localization.

proof.text: For a sheaf $M$ on $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, [lem-cbc-proetale-sheafification-geometric-stalk] identifies the stalk of $j_!M=P_M^\#$ with the colimit of $P_M(V)$ over the pointed neighbourhoods of [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. When $\bar x$ lies in $U$, the refinement $V\times_X U$ is a pointed neighbourhood factoring through $U$ by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Every representative restricts to this refinement. If two representatives become equal in the full colimit, filteredness gives a pointed neighbourhood on which they agree; refining that neighbourhood by its fibre product with $U$ gives the same equality among neighbourhoods factoring through $U$. Thus the map from the restricted colimit to the full colimit is both surjective and injective; there $P_M=M$ by [def-weil-extension-by-zero], and the index is precisely the pointed neighbourhood index in $U$. When $\bar x$ lies outside $U$, every pointed neighbourhood fails to factor through $U$, so every $P_M(V)$ is zero and its colimit is zero. These identifications commute with maps of $M$ because each colimit map comes from the component maps of $P_M$.

source.place: Proof, stalk-description sentence; agent representative-class cofinality argument using lem-cbc-proetale-sheafification-geometric-stalk, sourced at proetale.tex Section 0991 (section-points), Tags 0F6B (lemma-cofinal-etale), 0F6C (lemma-geometric-lift-to-cover), and sites.tex Tag 00Y8 (lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf), clause (3).

proof.text: For $A\to B$, restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] keeps every section group and restriction map, changing the action to $a\cdot m=\varphi(a)m$. Hence $P_{\operatorname{Res}M}$ and $\operatorname{Res}P_M$ have identical underlying abelian presheaves and identical $A_X$-actions. Module sheafification in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] is underlying abelian sheafification with the unique extended action; therefore the identity induces the claimed natural scalar comparison. The component maps on morphisms in [def-weil-extension-by-zero] agree as well. Apply $j_!$ and this identity in each degree, with differential $j_!(d^q)$. Exactness from Step 1 implies $\mathcal H^q(j_!K)=j_!\mathcal H^q(K)$, so quasi-isomorphisms are preserved and the termwise functor descends to the localization of cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], applied to the pro-etale module-sheaf category of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The same kernel-and-image argument for the exact restriction functor of Step 1 shows that it too preserves quasi-isomorphisms. The degreewise unit and counit are chain maps by naturality with respect to each differential. Their naturality for a quasi-isomorphism also gives naturality for its inverse after localization: multiply the naturality equation by the two inverted images. Thus they define natural transformations on the localization, where their degreewise triangle identities remain equalities. These are the unit and counit of the derived adjunction. Step 2 in each degree is the displayed stalk formula for complexes.
